precepts.text: One: at the Red Sea. Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? It had been better for us to serve the Egyptians.
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Numbers 14:22 says they “have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice”. These ten times are the countless acts of stubbornness of the children of Israel, and that is why the Lord asked “How long will this people provoke me?” Write them down. The Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

Number one is at the Red Sea. “And they said unto Moses, Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? wherefore hast thou dealt thus with us, to carry us forth out of Egypt? Is not this the word that we did tell thee in Egypt, saying, Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians? For it had been better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness.”

They were complaining to Moses. The Lord had just brought them out with his glory and his miracles, and the first thing they did at the sea was wish themselves back in Egypt serving the Egyptians.

precepts.text: Two: at Marah. The waters were bitter, and the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number two of the ten times the children of Israel tempted the Lord is at Marah, m-a-r-a-h. Write it down so you are not confused if it comes up again.

“And when they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter: therefore the name of it was called Marah. And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?”

The people complained because the water was bitter. They had just seen the Lord overthrow the Egyptians in the midst of the sea, and at the first bitter water they murmured against Moses. That is the provoking the Lord speaks of in Numbers 14:22: men “which have seen my glory, and my miracles”, and still did not hearken to his voice.

precepts.text: Three: the wilderness of Sin. The whole congregation murmured: would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots.
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number three is the wilderness of Sin. “And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness”. Do you notice a trend here?

“Would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.”

It is going to be the same thing when Christ comes back, but Christ is not playing games with us this time; he did not play games back then either. This time it will be ten times worse, ten times more severe, ten times more strict. When we are saved out of this modern day Egypt, Babylon the Great, America, the United Snakes of America, and Christ brings us into the wilderness, that grace is finished. No more I should have, could have, would have, I made a mistake. That is over with.

precepts.text: Four: hoarding the manna. Moses gave specific instruction, let no man leave of it till the morning; notwithstanding they hearkened not, and it bred worms and stank.
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number four is the hoarding of the manna. “And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning.” Moses gave specific instructions: do not leave any of the manna until the morning.

“Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.” Moses just told you. And they said, the hell with you; we want to replace you anyway. That is the mindset of our people.

This is what the Lord means in Numbers 14:22 when he says they “have not hearkened to my voice.” He fed them bread from heaven, gave one plain instruction, and they would not keep it.

precepts.text: Five: gathering on the Sabbath. The Lord gave two days of bread on the sixth day, and they went out on the seventh anyway. How long refuse ye to keep my commandments? No gratitude at all.
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number five is the Sabbath manna. “And it came to pass, that there went out some of the people on the seventh day for to gather, and they found none. And the Lord said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws? See, for that the Lord hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.”

They were supposed to gather extra on the sixth day; the Most High gave them enough manna to lay up for two days. And they said, no, Lord, we are going out on the seventh day to get this manna. Forgetting everything the Most High did for us in bringing us up out of Egypt. No gratitude. We are a people of no gratitude at all.

precepts.text: Six: Massah and Meribah. Chide means to be contentious, to go back and forth. They were almost ready to stone Moses over water, and the place was named for the chiding of the children of Israel, because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not?
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number six is at Massah and Meribah. “Wherefore the people did chide with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink.” To chide means to murmur, to be contentious, to go back and forth. “And Moses said unto them, Why chide ye with me? wherefore do ye tempt the Lord?”

Then, “the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst? And Moses cried unto the Lord, saying, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me.” They were almost ready to stone the man who brought them out of Egypt, over water.

The Lord said, “Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink.” And Moses “called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not?”

That is the very word Numbers 14:22 uses: they have “tempted me now these ten times.” The place itself was named for it.

precepts.text: Seven: the golden calf. As for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him: listen to the disrespect toward the man who led them out. Aaron made the calf out of fear, knowing better as high priest, and the people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play in honour of a god that cannot talk. No difference from our people today who prefer white Jesus or run to a stone in the east that cannot answer prayers.
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number seven is the golden calf. “And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.”

That is the no gratitude. The Most High just showed all those wonderful plagues and destroyed your enemy, and now you want a different god, a god of silver, gold and wood, a god that cannot talk. And look how disrespectful: as for this Moses. No different from our people who despise this truth and want to go back to Christianity, who prefer white Jesus, or who run to the east, to Mecca, and pray to a damn cobblestone that cannot talk back or answer prayers. That is why the Most High says we are dumber than an ox.

Aaron, the high priest, got real simple here, but it was out of fear, and he knew better. Then, “he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf”; he had the skills of a blacksmith and turned the gold they spoiled from Egypt into idolatry. It was the people who said “These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” Then “the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play”: in honour of that pagan god they had orgies.

“They have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them”. “I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people: Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them”. Yes, we are a stiffnecked people, and only Moses standing in the gap turned it away, as he did again in Numbers 14.

precepts.text: Eight: Taberah. When the people complained, it displeased the Lord, and the fire of the Lord burnt among them; the same thing he is going to do in America. Nine: the lusting for flesh. We remember the fish, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlick; ungrateful, complaining about the manna of heaven.
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number eight is Taberah. “And when the people complained, it displeased the Lord: and the Lord heard it; and his anger was kindled; and the fire of the Lord burnt among them, and consumed them that were in the uttermost parts of the camp.” More complaining, and the Most High started burning people with fire, the same thing he is going to do in America. “And the people cried unto Moses; and when Moses prayed unto the Lord, the fire was quenched.”

Then the lusting for flesh: “the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat? We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick”. Always about food; black people for you.

“But now our soul is dried away: there is nothing at all, beside this manna, before our eyes.” Ungrateful, complaining about the manna. Over and over the Lord was longsuffering, and over and over Moses prayed and the Lord pardoned, as Numbers 14:20 says: “I have pardoned according to thy word”.

precepts.text: And he called the name of that place Kibrothhattaavah: because there they buried the people that lusted.
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number nine: the lusting for flesh ended in a graveyard. “And he called the name of that place Kibroth–hattaavah: because there they buried the people that lusted.” Taberah was number eight; Kibroth-hattaavah is number nine.

Number ten is the report of the spies, the doubt and fear of Numbers 13 and 14, and there the Most High had enough. “Surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers, neither shall any of them that provoked me see it”. Everyone twenty and upward fell in the wilderness, save Caleb and Joshua.

The Most High deals in numbers, and everything in the Bible is significant. Ten times he was longsuffering, and places like Kibroth-hattaavah still carry the names of what our fathers did.

precepts.text: How long shall I bear with this evil congregation? When we came out of Egypt, our people were evil. You thought they were righteous? They were rebellious: liars, fornicators, murmurers. Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness, from twenty years old and upward. Once you were 20 years old and up, the Lord said, all of you are going to die. Even Aaron died, and Moses did not enter; not that Moses was evil, but the people provoked him to anger. Joshua and Caleb were the only two adults the Lord allowed to make it into the promised land. Everybody 20 and up, their blood was on their own head, because according to the law, at 20 you are the age of a man and you take responsibility for yourself. The little ones which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in. The children wandered 40 years and bore the whoredoms of the adults, until every last rebellious one died. That is what the Lord did to us in the wilderness: he purged that leaven out of our people.
precepts.point: It shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the Lord's law may be in thy mouth. Why are we celebrating the days of unleavened bread? It is a sign for us to keep God's laws, for God's laws to be in our minds. That is what the days of unleavened bread really represent.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

precepts.why:
Exodus 13:8 says “And thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the Lord did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt.” This is done means the feast of unleavened bread. But what did the Lord do unto me? The Lord delivered everyone, but did everyone enter the promised land? No. Numbers 14 shows what he did.

“How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me?” When we came out of Egypt, our people were evil. You thought they were righteous? They were rebellious: a bunch of liars, fornicators, murmurers. The Lord said, “as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward”. Once you were twenty years old and up, the Lord said, all of you are going to die. Aaron died. Moses died too; not that Moses was evil, but the people provoked him to anger, so he did not see the promised land, though when he left his body he was going back to paradise.

“Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.” Joshua and Caleb were the only two adults the Lord allowed to make it in. According to the law, at twenty you are the age of a man and take responsibility for yourself, which is why twenty is the age to marry. Everybody twenty and up, their blood was on their own head.

“But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised.” The children wandered forty years and bore the whoredoms of the adults, seeing all the evil they did, “until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness”: until every last one of those wicked Israelites died, everybody who had leaven in them, the murmurers, the adulterers, the ones who held on to Egypt.

So the me of Exodus 13:8 is not Moses. It is the little ones, twenty years and under, who grew up in the land and told their sons: we keep unleavened bread because the Lord purged the leaven out of me in the wilderness. And it is the same in the future: whoever keeps leaven, which is sin, through the seven days, that soul shall be cut off.

precepts.text: After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years.
precepts.point: He shall confirm the covenant with many for one week, and in the midst of the week cause the sacrifice and oblation to cease, with the overspreading of abominations in the temple that Christ warned of. All seventy weeks are fulfilled. Amalek tells Christians the last week is future and belongs to a rebuilt temple, counting on blacks and Latinos not understanding the scriptures.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
Edom twists Daniel 9, so here is the code to break it down. Write it down: each day represents one year, each week represents seven years, and seventy weeks is 490 years. How do we know? Start with why Israel spent forty years in the wilderness.

“After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years”. The spies searched the land forty days. Because Israel sinned, they bore their iniquity forty years in the wilderness, a year for every day. “and ye shall know my breach of promise”: the Lord told them not to go up there, and they went up anyway.

That is the Lord himself counting a day for a year. So when Daniel is told “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”, those weeks are counted the same way: seventy weeks of seven days, every day a year, 490 years.

precepts.text: The Lord is longsuffering and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity, and by no means clearing the guilty.
precepts.point: Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers. Our help is in the name of the Lord.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
“The Lord is longsuffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression”. Being longsuffering is one of the characteristics we must take on with our brothers and our sisters. A lot of times we are carnal and have no patience with each other. A brother offends you, or does what you think is an offence that he may not even see as one, and you get all in your feelings; sisters get in their feelings about something somebody said or the way somebody moves toward them. We are all different spirits joining together for one common goal. We are not all going to get along, but we all have to be longsuffering with each other and endure it.

Then: “and by no means clearing the guilty”. Why is he of great mercy but will by no means clear the guilty? Just because you sin and are not judged immediately does not mean you will not be judged; you are still guilty of that sin. And to get that great mercy, you have to repent and forsake your sins. The ones he will not clear are those that do not repent, and he visits “the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation.”

So back to Psalms 124: it is of the Lord’s mercy, longsuffering with Israel, that the men who rose up against us did not swallow us up.

precepts.text: Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven; Moses' intercession loosed the judgment, and the Lord pardoned according to his word.
precepts.point: Moses interceded: the Egyptians and the nations would hear that the Lord was not able to bring the people into the land and slew them in the wilderness. He pleaded, Let the power of my Lord be great, the Lord is longsuffering and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity; pardon this people according to the greatness of thy mercy, as thou hast forgiven them from Egypt until now. This is a true leader interceding for the people rather than seeing them destroyed.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

precepts.why:
The Lord said He would smite the people with the pestilence and disinherit them and make of Moses a greater nation. Moses interceded instead: the Egyptians and the nations would say “Because the Lord was not able to bring this people into the land which he sware unto them, therefore he hath slain them in the wilderness.” He pleaded, “let the power of my Lord be great”, “The Lord is longsuffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression”, and “Pardon, I beseech thee, the iniquity of this people according unto the greatness of thy mercy, and as thou hast forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now.”

“Verily I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.” Moses' intercession loosed the judgment on earth, and the Lord pardoned according to his word.

This is a true leader interceding for the people rather than seeing them destroyed, and what the man of God loosed on earth was loosed in heaven.

precepts.text: Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer; now all these things happened unto them for ensamples, and are written for our admonition.
precepts.point: The little ones they said would be a prey, those He would bring into the land; but the children would wander in the wilderness forty years, a year for each of the forty days the land was searched, and bear the whoredoms of their fathers until their carcasses were wasted. The very men that brought up the evil report died by the plague before the Lord, but Joshua and Caleb lived still.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

precepts.why:
“I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against me.” For that murmuring the Lord swore, “Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness”, all that were numbered from twenty years old and upward, save Caleb and Joshua; and the men that brought up the evil report “died by the plague before the Lord.”

Paul takes it straight to us: “Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer. Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.”

The carcases in the wilderness are an ensample written for our admonition. The same murmuring brings the same destroyer, and we are the ones upon whom the ends of the world are come.

precepts.text: Harden not your hearts as in the provocation in the wilderness; take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God.
precepts.point: The little ones they said would be a prey, those He would bring into the land; but the children would wander in the wilderness forty years, a year for each of the forty days the land was searched, and bear the whoredoms of their fathers until their carcasses were wasted. The very men that brought up the evil report died by the plague before the Lord, but Joshua and Caleb lived still.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

precepts.why:
The children would “wander in the wilderness forty years”, a year for each of the forty days the land was searched, “until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness.” Hebrews calls that generation by name.

“Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness: When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years. Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do alway err in their heart; and they have not known my ways. So I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.” The oath of Numbers 14, that they should not come into the land, is the oath that they shall not enter into His rest.

“Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.” The provocation in the wilderness was an evil heart of unbelief, and the warning is to us, that we harden not our hearts as they did.

precepts.text: None that provoked the Lord shall see the land, but Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and followed the Lord fully, shall possess it.
precepts.point: Let that be a lesson learned, for whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

note.label: Numbers 26: The Second Census of the Families of Israel

precepts.why:
Of all the men numbered in the wilderness of Sinai, “there was not left a man of them, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.” Why Caleb and Joshua? They had another spirit on them and did not doubt when the Lord sent them to spy out the land.

“Surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers, neither shall any of them that provoked me see it: But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land whereinto he went; and his seed shall possess it.”

None that provoked the Lord saw the land; Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and followed the Lord fully, went in and his seed possessed it. He let nobody keep him from serving the Most High.

So if you read in Acts how Theudas drew away four hundred men, how do you know not to go along with whatever that heresy is? God says there has to be another spirit within you. And that spirit is already there. It was ordained of God from the very beginning.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

points: And Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, which were of them that searched the land, rent their clothes.

For they are bread for us. They said, they are food for us, we can take them by the power of the Lord. It said Joshua and Caleb rent their clothes, meaning they were furious and sorrowful for the false report that was given. So Joshua and Caleb did have a different kind of spirit on them, because they did not go with the general populace with their false report. How do you know not to go along with what a populace is saying when it is contrary to the Lord? The spirit of God must be upon you.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

points: And they spake unto all the company of the children of Israel, saying, The land, which we passed through to search it, is an exceeding good land.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

points: If the Lord delight in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it us; a land which floweth with milk and honey. There were spies sent out, and Joshua and Caleb were part of that group. The report that Joshua and Caleb brought back was that they could take the land. But the others brought back an evil report. They were deceptive, they tried to diminish the power of the Lord, and the Lord judged them for it.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

points: Only rebel not ye against the Lord, neither fear ye the people of the land; for they are bread for us: their defence is departed from them, and the Lord is with us: fear them not. Joshua and Caleb are telling the congregation of Israel, we can take this land through the power of the Lord. The only stipulation that will cause us not to get this land is if we rebel against the Lord. Is that the same with us? We have an inheritance that the Lord ordained for us, and the only stipulation is, do not rebel against the Lord.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

points: But all the congregation bade stone them with stones. And the glory of the Lord appeared in the tabernacle of the congregation before all the children of Israel. So these two men that had the spirit of God upon them, that understood what God's mission was for the nation of Israel, encouraged them: listen, we have to go take this land that the Lord ordained for us, he did not bring us out of Egypt not to obtain the land. And they said, let us stone these guys, let us kill them, instead of doing what God said.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

points: All the congregation lifted up their voice and cried, and murmured against Moses and against Aaron: would God that we had died in the land of Egypt! And they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Let us return to slavery: that is a slave mentality. They got freedom and wanted to go back to the house of bondage. It is the same mentality now with those who say this land of captivity is home. We were brought here; this is exile, not home. Our home is Jerusalem. Taking pride in the identity of Babylon over the identity God gave you is blasphemy.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: The spirit of fear jumped from the leaders onto everybody: all the congregation lifted up their voice and cried, and all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron. When they murmured against Moses and Aaron, who were they truly murmuring against? The instruction came from the Most High.

Would God that we had died in Egypt; were it not better for us to return into Egypt? In chapter one of this history they were crying to the Most High under the taskmasters; now they are in the wilderness and want to go back to master. Remember Harriet Tubman: I could have saved thousands more if they had known they were slaves. Our people still want to stay with master in Babylon America; it is the same thought.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: And they said one to another, Let us make a captain. No to the leaders God appointed; they wanted somebody to give heed unto their itching ears.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: The Lord said unto Moses, How long will this people provoke me? and how long will it be ere they believe me, for all the signs which I have shewed among them? The Most High is showing longsuffering: all the plagues, all the miracles, and they are still moved by unbelief.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: The Lord is longsuffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression, and by no means clearing the guilty. Moses stood as the mediator between us and God, and the Lord said, I have pardoned according to thy word. That is how much the Most High loved Israel and loved Moses.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: The tenth provocation was the report of the spies, and it was the last: how long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me? Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun, because Caleb had another spirit with him and followed the Lord fully.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: Those twenty years old and upward did not enter in; the little ones the doubters said would be a prey were the ones brought in to know the land their fathers despised.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years. That is how the Most High gets down with numbers: the forty years matched the forty days exactly.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: All those men which have seen my glory and my miracles: we saw his glory in the way the sea split, we saw the pillar give us light at night, we saw all the plagues when Moses went before Pharaoh.
And have tempted me now these ten times: in the wilderness we tested God ten times already, and have not hearkened to my voice. Surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land. Out of all the people that came out of Egypt, only Caleb and Joshua saw that land; the men that came out died in the wilderness and their children went in. That is how rebellious we were, and that is how rebellious we still are.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: When we were in Egypt, were we loved by the Egyptians? No. The same way we are hated in America, we were hated in Egypt also. Yet the whole congregation said, would God that we had died in the land of Egypt; were it not better for us to return into Egypt?

Some of us have it good here. America has spoiled some of us; that is why some of you never go anywhere but stay here. It was the same in Egypt: the taskmasters had it good. Look at the so-called black leaders and politicians today: some have been in Congress for over 30 years and never done one thing for the black community. Pastors living in multimillion dollar houses and flying private jets do not want America to fall.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: And they said one to another, let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt. They basically said, let us remove Moses, raise up another leader, and go back. Ten plagues it took for Pharaoh to let us go, and they said, we do not care, let us go back to Egypt. That is how rebellious we are as a people, but yet we are complaining about why they hate us.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: All the congregation lifted up their voice and cried, and the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron: would God that we had died in the land of Egypt. Same thing again. Now, mind you, who are they saying this to? God.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: And they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt. Them imaginations. Let's set up our own leader and go back to Egypt.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: The simple right now is saying, well, how did they despise the land? They just wanted water and food. You don't bite the hand that feeds you. The same hand that's going to give you that land, you had better make sure you taking care of business and doing what that hand wants you to do. If you murmur, complain, talebear, gossip, guess what's going to happen? The Lord said he going to kill you. Oh, y'all thought it was a game.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: How long shall I bear with this evil congregation? Wait a minute. The Lord, yes, he runs out of patience too. He was patient when they asked for water. He was patient when they asked for food. He gave it to them, but that wasn't good enough. What did Israel continue to do? Complain, complain, complain.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: As truly as I live, saith the Lord, as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you. Okay, keep on asking for it then. I would to God we had died in Egypt; I would to God we had died in the wilderness. What he say? So will I do to you.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; all that were numbered of you, from twenty years old and upward, which have murmured against me. Now he getting real specific. Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun. But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron. So, murmuring, complaining, was one of the sins that the children of Israel committed.

And the whole congregation said unto them, Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt! or would God we had died in this wilderness! So it is not for the Lord delivering us from our enemies — that was not good enough. It is not that the Lord gave us manna to eat. He gave us water to drink. The manna tasted like whatever it is that you wanted it to taste like. That was not enough.
We continued to murmur and complain against Moses and Aaron. Against the Lord — which was inevitably against the Lord.

note.label: Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: And they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt. These dudes were trying to set up a coup. They were trying to — that is called sedition. That is sedition. Let us look up sedition.

note.label: Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: But all the congregation bade stone them with stones. And the glory of the Lord appeared in the tabernacle of the congregation before all the children of Israel.
Moses and Aaron were lawful authority. But Israel was like, I do not care about that.
And they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt. They said, listen, let us move Moses out of the way. Let us set up a leader — and let us go back to captivity.

You have got to be mindful of that spirit. When you have brothers and sisters, when you are going against authorised authority, or lawful authority — authority that was set up by the Most High God and his son, Jesus the Christ — that is a sure sign of a seditious spirit.

note.label: Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: All the congregation lifted up their voice and cried, and the people wept that night, and murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying, Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt, or in this wilderness.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

points: Because of the evil report, they said, Wherefore hath the LORD brought us unto this land, to fall by the sword? and they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt, forgetting there was nothing to return to, for Pharaoh and his army were destroyed and Egypt laid waste.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

points: Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before all the assembly, and Joshua and Caleb rent their clothes and exhorted the people: the land is an exceeding good land; if the Lord delight in us, He will bring us into it; only rebel not against the Lord, neither fear the people of the land, for they are bread for us, and the Lord is with us.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

points: But all the congregation bade stone them with stones, and the glory of the Lord appeared in the tabernacle. It is the same today: when the truth is brought that the Most High loves the people and has something great for them if they repent, they do not believe it and are ready to kill the messenger, hating him that rebuketh in the gate.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

points: The Lord said, How long will this people provoke me? and how long will it be ere they believe me, for all the signs which I have shewed among them? He would smite them with pestilence, disinherit them, and make of Moses a greater nation.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

points: Moses interceded: the Egyptians and the nations would hear that the Lord was not able to bring the people into the land and slew them in the wilderness. He pleaded, Let the power of my Lord be great, the Lord is longsuffering and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity; pardon this people according to the greatness of thy mercy, as thou hast forgiven them from Egypt until now. This is a true leader interceding for the people rather than seeing them destroyed.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

points: The Lord said, I have pardoned according to thy word; but as truly as I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord. The men who had seen His glory and His miracles in Egypt and in the wilderness, and had tempted Him now these ten times, would not see the land which He sware unto their fathers.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

points: But His servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and followed the Lord fully, would be brought into the land, and his seed should possess it.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

points: The Lord asked how long He should bear with this evil congregation which murmured against Him, and declared, As ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: your carcasses shall fall in this wilderness, all that were numbered from twenty years old and upward that murmured against Him, save Caleb and Joshua.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

points: The little ones they said would be a prey, those He would bring into the land; but the children would wander in the wilderness forty years, a year for each of the forty days the land was searched, and bear the whoredoms of their fathers until their carcasses were wasted. The very men that brought up the evil report died by the plague before the Lord, but Joshua and Caleb lived still.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

points: When Moses told the people these sayings, they mourned greatly, then rose up early and presumed to go up to the top of the mountain, saying, We have sinned; we will go up unto the place which the Lord hath promised.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

points: Moses said, Wherefore now do ye transgress the commandment of the LORD? it shall not prosper; go not up, for the LORD is not among you, that ye be not smitten before your enemies. But they presumed to go up, though the ark of the covenant and Moses departed not out of the camp, and the Amalekites and the Canaanites came down and smote them and discomfited them, even unto Hormah.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned
